finding.claim: Authorization bypass on file deletion. `require_allowed` is an alias for the boolean `is_allowed`, not the aborting `ensure_allowed`. Its return value is discarded, so the 'delete' check never blocks anyone. Any requester can delete any file.
finding.source: Any HTTP client sending DELETE /files/<fid> with an arbitrary or missing user header and a known fid.

trace.note: `from acl import is_allowed as require_allowed` aliases the non-aborting boolean function
`require_allowed(g.user, f, "delete")` returns False but the result is ignored, so no abort(403)
`is_allowed` only returns a bool and never raises

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the ignored boolean call. `rename_file` correctly uses `ensure_allowed`, which aborts. There is no other auth middleware; `before_request` only populates g.user and never rejects.

verdict.guard_found: Only views.py:18 require_allowed(...), which is the boolean acl.is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) with its result discarded; before_request (views.py:10-12) only sets g.user and never rejects. No effective control.
verdict.reason: views.py:4 aliases the non-aborting boolean is_allowed (acl.py:5) as require_allowed, views.py:18 discards its result, so views.py:19 `del STORE[fid]` runs for any requester, including anonymous ones with no user header, who know a valid fid.

finding.claim: Identity is taken from a client-supplied header. The name 'X-Session-User-Verified' suggests it was verified, but nothing verifies it. Any caller can impersonate any user, including a grantee of 'write' or 'delete', and defeat the ACL on rename (and on delete once F1 is fixed).

trace.note: `g.user = request.headers.get("X-Session-User-Verified")` with no session, signature or token validation
The grants lookup is keyed on the attacker-chosen username
The rename is performed as the impersonated user

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, session, signature or trusted-proxy stripping of the header is present in the code. Whether an upstream proxy strips or sets the header cannot be determined from this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none in repo. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) aborts 403 correctly, but it checks grants keyed on the spoofed identity. No authentication, signature check or header stripping exists. Whether an upstream proxy strips the header can't be seen from the repo.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 sets g.user straight from the client header, and acl.py:5 looks up grants by that string, so an anonymous caller who sends the name of a user holding "write" passes ensure_allowed at views.py:26 and renames at views.py:27.
